Balanced integer product maximizes, explicit same-orthant finite pair realizes the bound. Scalar ReLU one-point edgewise contraction and the two asymptotic regimes follow exactly. Code independently checks 2,552 mask eigenvalues, norming directions and rational identities; numerical tests do not prove infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Nine actual semantic published-record searches and recoverable historical claims were compared at the level of mathematical implication. Closest entries concern either different norms (Lipschitz-free spaces, standard lp geometry, graph total variation) or a different operation. Full primary-text comparison of Cai--Wang's one-point Dirichlet-energy contraction (Lemma 3.3) reveals no sharp two-point Lipschitz modulus; finite graph threshold dynamics and continuum truncation sources likewise do not establish the complete-graph mask formula. The combination of all-coupling exact norm and balanced-orthant attainment was not covered by the inspected sources; unindexed earlier finite-matrix computations remain a risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent result may be buried in classical finite-dimensional Nemytskii operator or quadratic norm/coordinate-mask literature not indexed by the examined searches.
Search records provide ranked summaries rather than full published packages; closest comparisons were also cross-checked with accessible prior claim material.

value.rationale: Graph-energy truncation is standard in threshold dynamics and ReLU processing, where one-point Dirichlet-energy decrease can misleadingly suggest perturbation nonexpansion. This theorem gives the exact sharp global two-point stability constant for every graph size and coupling, identifies all locally norming sign-mask proportions, and separates bounded coupling-per-vertex regimes from order-sqrt(n) instability at fixed edge coupling. This natural complete-graph benchmark quantifies conditioning not supplied by the graph-energy contraction lemma; its precise all-parameter constant is the meaningful invariant, not an arbitrary small-dimensional computation.
